rounds.text: Srivari Spices & Foods Ltd faces significant liquidity and operational risks that undermine its recent growth narrative. Despite reported profits, the company generated negative operating cash flow of Rs -14 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -15 Cr in March 2026 [E23, E24]. This disconnect is highlighted by a cash conversion ratio of -0.88x, meaning operating cash flow was -44% of reported profit [E22, E25]. Furthermore, the company’s working capital efficiency is deteriorating, as evidenced by debtor days increasing from 104 to 126 days [E48]. The financial position is further pressured by a doubling of borrowings from Rs 17 Cr to Rs 34 Cr within a single year [E28]. Conceded: the company maintains a comfortable current ratio of 2.50x [E27] and has demonstrated strong historical ROE and ROCE metrics [E9, E10]. However, the substantial reduction in promoter holdings from 69.94% to 58.28% over the last two years warrants caution regarding long-term alignment [E30].
